codebook:
structure    flat-chain (reads as one list of conditions tried in order: every nested ternary
               in the alternate) | nested (a decision inside a decision: a ternary in a
               consequent or a test)
  reads        better | same | worse: the rewrite chosen below (or, for keep, the best statement
               rewrite) against the ternary as written
  rewrite      early-return | if-else (let plus if/else, or if/else statements) | helper (a
               function or variable above) | lookup (an object or Map) | switch |
               component-split (JSX: an early return in the component or a child component) |
               keep (the ternary is the clearest form here)
  lookupSafe   yes (a lookup would behave the same for every value that reaches it) | no (it
               would evaluate a call or a read that can throw, change a nullish branch, or match
               an inherited key) | n/a (the tests don't compare one value with constants)
  notes        one line

rater1.notes: config enum 'always'/'never' else shouldInlineAsset(); a lookup keeps the call lazy behind ??, values are booleans, inlineConfig is a closed union; the formatted chain is about as clear
arrow-key swap on event.key; key is an open string, so a plain-object lookup could match inherited keys
branches run .every() over element lists; a lookup would run both scans eagerly
kind is a closed union mapped to one-character constants: a textbook lookup
typeof dispatch; a lookup would call params(data) eagerly and throw when params isn't a function
three 15-line JSX states keyed on renderedStatus; eager lookup would build every state and call getCurrentLocationUrl()

rater2.notes: Three status panels over 50 lines with a hidden null tail; a child component switching on renderedStatus with early returns reads better. The inner spaFromUrl/spaToUrl ternaries are optional rows, not a second decision. A lookup would eagerly build all panels and call getCurrentLocationUrl, which cannot throw, so it behaves the same.

rater1.notes: status enum to Badge label/variant; the elements are plain and the default covers unknown statuses
minify is 'oxc' | false | …; a lookup would have to key on the boolean false through string coercion

rater2.notes: Short two-step mapping of minify ('oxc' -> true, false -> 'dce-only', else undefined) inside an options object; hoisting a let/if-else is about equal. A Map or object keyed by the closed minify values (false coerces to "false") behaves the same.

rater1.notes: the '*' branch increments matchId; a lookup would increment it for every segment
four-way enum dispatch to scrollbar components with null default; a switch on context.type reads better
textAlign union to anchor ratio; short line, a lookup is no harder to read

rater2.notes: One-line alignment-to-ratio mapping in an arrow that returns an object literal; statements would need a block body and lets. A {left:0,center:0.5,right:1} table over the closed textAlign union would be equivalent but no clearer.

rater1.notes: enum to constant metadata in a hot loop; values are constant enum members

rater2.notes: Two-case enum-to-flag mapping with a 0 default in a hot loop; a let plus if/else is the same length and loses const. A lookup keyed by the numeric enum values would behave the same.

rater1.notes: the a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0 comparator idiom; a block would be noisier

rater2.notes: The standard inline sort comparator (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0); a block-body comparator with ifs is noisier. The tests are relational, not value-vs-constant.

rater1.notes: guard (missing elements return 0) then one ternary

rater2.notes: The whole function is one return whose first arm is a guard (missing element -> 0); `if (!a || !b) return 0; return isElementPreceding(...) ? -1 : 1` reads as a guard clause.

rater1.notes: decision inside a decision with a comment wedged into the alternate; a block callback with a guard reads better
two different headers compared with originDomain, object-literal branches, undefined default
value ?? defaultValue ?? [min, max] style fallback in a useMemo callback; idiomatic

rater2.notes: A clear priority fallback (value, else defaultValue, else [min, max]) in a useMemo arrow; early returns in a block body read about the same. The tests are Array.isArray calls.

rater1.notes: four-way provider icon choice inside a map callback that already has a block body

rater2.notes: A four-level stair in a map callback that already has a statement body; ifs that return read as a list. p is an open provider string, so an email/SAML lookup could match inherited keys, and the isCustom call has to run first.

rater1.notes: small comparator inside an if; a guard plus one ternary is no clearer
scoring callback; early returns in a block body are about as clear

rater2.notes: The ternary sits in the consequent of the equality test. A block-body callback with `if (lines differ) return 0.99;` and then a single length ternary flattens it.

rater1.notes: proxy getter: if (prop !== 'key') return value, then the shift-key ternary; the comment inside the ternary goes away

rater2.notes: The shiftKey ternary is in the consequent, with a comment wedged between ? and the inner test. The Proxy get handler already has statements, so `if (prop !== "key") return value;` then the case flip reads better.

rater1.notes: the JSDoc lists the rules in order; early returns mirror it
dense ternary in a map callback inside a template inside new RegExp; a named helper per literal reads better

rater2.notes: A dense per-literal escape inside map, inside a template literal, inside a ternary, inside new RegExp. A named escapeLiteral helper above, giving `vals.map(escapeLiteral).join("|")`, reads better. The tests are typeof and truthiness checks.

rater1.notes: if (!image.complete) return Loading, then one ternary
three path cases documented in the JSDoc; early returns read as the list

rater2.notes: The function body is a single return with a negated middle test (_page !== '/index' ? _page : '/'). Early returns let '/index' -> '/' be stated positively. The first test is a call, not a constant comparison.

rater1.notes: map callback choosing one of three large components; second test adds a plan check, so not a lookup
collapses to one condition: isSharedFile && !isUnmanagedFile ? '' : undefined
pointerEvents style value with an undefined default; a variable above is no clearer
three large JSX branches with inline handlers; a content variable built with if/else reads better

rater2.notes: Three UI states (editing input, link, empty) as a flat JSX chain. Its handlers close over many locals, so a child component or a hoisted let/if-else moves the code without making it clearer.

rater1.notes: placeholder / bar chart / null inside a panel; a variable above is about the same

rater2.notes: Two-step JSX chain (no config -> placeholder, bar -> chart, else null). A child component with early returns is about equal. The ResizablePanel nested inside a ResizablePanel is a separate oddity.

rater1.notes: spread of one of three CSS-variable objects; a function returning the size vars reads better

rater2.notes: Three size modes as a 20-line spread inside a style object, with the panel-width expression repeated. A getPanelSizeVars() helper with early returns reads better. The inner `x ? px : undefined` ternaries are only value formatting.

rater1.notes: three render paths each with an explanatory comment; the ternary keeps the comments next to their branch

rater2.notes: Three clear cases on two booleans (raw children, slot onto the child, wrap) with an explanatory comment; a hoisted let content with if/else reads about the same.

rater1.notes: eight unrelated flags choosing an icon; a getIcon() with early returns reads better
placeholder with a compound test and a template holding another ternary; compute it above

rater2.notes: The placeholder prop combines a compound OR test (including a typeof check) with another ternary inside the template literal. A getPlaceholder(field) helper with early returns reads better. The tests are not a single value against constants.

rater1.notes: snippet line rendering: parts / highlighted / plain; a render helper is about the same

rater2.notes: A short three-way snippet render (parts, highlighted, plain) inside a map; a SnippetLine child component with early returns would be about equal.

rater1.notes: one slot in a row of toolbar buttons; moving it out breaks the visual order
the tree is a chain, but its first branch holds another ternary (error ? … : tabs) in JSX: reads as nested; a response panel component

rater2.notes: The response branch holds its own error-vs-tabs decision, an 80-line tree. A ResponseView child with `if (error) return ...` plus early returns for the pending and empty states reads better.

rater1.notes: small optional badge in a row; turning it into two && would render both, a variable above moves it away
picks one of three translation keys inline in t(); kind and shiftKey are different tests
loading / empty / content: the common three-state render

rater2.notes: A small loading/empty/content JSX chain. The negated `!description ?` is mild, and a child component for three tiny states is not clearer.

rater1.notes: multi-value variant test then an unrelated flag; a getExplanation helper reads better

rater2.notes: Two arms with well-named constants and an undefined tail. A helper with early returns is equal, not clearer. The second test is a different field (inNavigation), so a lookup on variant doesn't cover it.

rater1.notes: category list / no match / null; the list branch is long
tooltip reason from three negated permission flags; a helper with early returns reads better

rater2.notes: A four-arm stair of negated flags ending in undefined, buried in tooltip.content.text. A named disabled-reason helper with early returns reads as a list and pairs with the disabled prop.

rater1.notes: first/last tick marker; second test compares index with a computed value, not a constant
four placeholder states, each a t() call; compute above

rater2.notes: Flat-formatted (unindented) chain of placeholder states that already reads as an ordered list; a helper with ifs is equivalent. The tests are on different values.

rater1.notes: skeleton / count / '0' / null with an includes() test; a render helper reads better

rater2.notes: A three-level JSX chain with a magic list (['log_type','method','level']) and a Map get. A named count-label helper or constant above, with early returns, reads better.

rater1.notes: minify resolution with a lib-format check nested in the 'oxc' branch and a comment inside an object branch

rater2.notes: The lib-ES check is nested in the 'oxc' consequent alongside a commented object literal. A resolveMinify helper with early returns reads better. A lookup on the closed minify values with ?? false would behave the same, since evaluating the inner arm can't throw.

rater1.notes: the next line returns regex, so early returns per precision case read better
three parallel one-line ternaries on before/after read as a table
normalise to an array: [] / value / [value]
read-only precedence nested inside the defined check with a multi-line filter; a helper with early returns
text-anchor from align and direction; second test is compound
one-line clamp with ternaries in both branches; a clamp helper or if/else reads better

rater2.notes: One long line with ternaries in both arms, mirrored for endColumn. A small clamp helper (or if/else with Math.max) used for start and end reads better. The tests compare lines with each other, not constants.

rater1.notes: instanceof chain to find the form; if/else with each case on its own reads better
string / array join / '' for textContent, already inside an if/else
the function returns !isNoColor next; early returns drop the eslint-disable comment from inside the ternary
array join nested under a truthiness check; small either way

rater2.notes: A guard-then-normalize idiom. A let with if/else is about equal. The real fix is a single ternary, `Array.isArray(x) ? x.join(' ') : x || undefined`, which removes the nesting with the same results.

rater1.notes: normalise input to an array: string / array / object values
build the checks array; three short cases
swipe direction from a prop or the position; short
one of several parallel five-deep status chains; derive the state once, then map it to messages

rater2.notes: A six-arm chain with an isUpgrade decision in one consequent, repeated across several copy lines. Deriving one phase in a helper with early returns, then mapping copy per phase, reads much better. The tests are separate booleans.

rater1.notes: margin by element-type predicate; three short cases
awaited ternary of three render calls; a let with if/else (or helper) separates the await

rater2.notes: Three render paths by fallback type, inside await(...). A renderFallback helper with early returns is about equal. The tests are type checks.

rater1.notes: the exact/inclusive phrase repeats in every locale message; one helper removes the repetition
one of four parallel per-side geometry expressions in an array; rewriting each loses the visible symmetry

rater2.notes: An OR test nested in the consequent, inside one of four parallel array entries, with an unindented old-Prettier layout. Naming the overlap tests and computing each bound above the array reads better. The tests are relational.

rater1.notes: normalise a header value to an array inside a spread

rater2.notes: The idiomatic normalize-header-to-array chain (string -> [s], array -> itself, else []); a hoisted let with if/else is about equal. The tests are typeof and Array.isArray.

rater1.notes: undo/redo reason buried in a long call inside an if; a const above reads better
configured breakpoints, else one of two constants by service
ssr / lib / false for one rolldown option

rater2.notes: A short two-boolean priority (ssr, lib, else false) as an option value; hoisting an if/else is no clearer.

rater1.notes: custom and granted are exclusive statuses, so it simplifies to isGranted ? !hasPendingRemove : hasPendingAdd

rater2.notes: The first and last arms are both hasPendingAdd, and custom/granted are exclusive statuses, so the chain collapses to `isGranted ? !hasPendingRemove : hasPendingAdd`. A statement rewrite of a boolean inside && would be worse.

rater1.notes: the chain sits inside the alternate of childStr === '' ? '' : …; a prefix variable with if/else in the callback (it reads c.#varIndex, so it stays in the class)

rater2.notes: A parenthesized chain concatenated with + childStr, in the alternate of the childStr === '' check. The map callback already has statements, so returns per case (empty, var index, meta char, plain) read better.

rater1.notes: same repeated exact/inclusive phrase as n64

rater2.notes: One-line exact/inclusive/exclusive wording inside a template literal; a statement rewrite needs a hoisted variable per branch. The duplication across branches is a separate issue.

rater1.notes: anchor ratio: centre / left / right in one call argument

rater2.notes: A one-line anchor ratio (center 0.5, dragged left 1, else 0) as an object argument; hoisting a let with if/else is noisier. The tests are a flag and a comparison.

rater1.notes: rendering mode nested under the app PPR flag, next to a sibling of the same shape
platform font family in a module-level constant; sibling fontSize is a ternary too
flag parsing; the second test simplifies to allowedHosts === true
merge minify options when both are objects
the same normalisation is written twice (definition, check); one helper
end index in a hot query-string loop; a let with if is no clearer
same repeated exact/inclusive phrase as n64

note: Rater 1 labelled all items from the worksheet with the census's automatic labels; rater 2, a separate subagent working blind, labelled the subset. Shares are rater 1's, weighted by each stratum's population (sample.json).
